text.text_excerpt: I've been here before while on vacation in the New Orleans French quarter. I've never had yoga like this before! It's a very beautiful studio overall. It has such a positive vibe here and a tracks a diverse range of people. The studios owner/instructor's name is Ajax. Her studio teaches Bikram yoga which is a style of yoga that involves practicing yoga at high temperatures. There are apparently good health benefits associated with this practice. The actual room where all the action happens is sweltering as she has the heater on also. All I can say is make sure you bring a towel and giant bottle of water and drink plenty of it ahead of time. I've tried yoga in the park, goat yoga, trap yoga, rooftop yoga, yoga and beer, yoga and blunts and nothing compares AT ALL to the experience I had at Magnolia Yoga Studio. Oftentimes when you come as a newcomer I'd be completely intimidated that wasn't the case this time. The owner actually taught our class and she was sooooo welcoming and patient and encouraging. Never did she make us feel like the completely uncoordinated beginners that we were. The space is magnificent, it has such a clean and positive energy that simply radiates throughout the studio. I can't wait to go back. If you're a local or just in town visiting for a few days and want to check them out you definitely should. I...

I have been dying to try Magnolia Yoga Studio and their 21DaysHotYoga Challenge was the perfect time for me to jump in and leave the excuses. I'm no novice to yoga but this was my first time doing hot yoga and I absolutely loved it. Ajax and her team of instructors are welcoming, knowledgeable, and extremely encouraging. This is a small studio with one yoga room (closed off from the common area) with a padded yoga floor, so you don't have to double up on mats and there are male and female lockers with showers.
